title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Public sector innovation procurement framework
sections.summary: The public sector could earmark tenders to promote innovation, and a new "buy innovation" procurement framework is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As a start, the public sector could earmark a portion of the public sector tenders specifically to promote and encourage innovation and creativity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government establish a new "buy innovation" procurement framework where innovative solutions are being sought for public sector problems.

sections.label: Scheme projects and take up
sections.summary: Despite being a $450-million scheme, only 28 projects were put up since 2011, with no mention of take up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Despite being a $450-million scheme, only 28 projects were put up since 2011, with no mention of any take up.

sections.label: Government co-creating solutions with businesses
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how the Government intends to co-create solutions with businesses and the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given the call in the Budget Statement for the Government to better partner industry and innovators, can the Minister share how the Government intends to co-create solutions with businesses and the public?

sections.label: Contract price escalation clauses
sections.summary: Escalation clauses raise contract prices by a pre-agreed formula when key costs rise, protecting contractors and reducing over-budgeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is a win-win for the Government and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These clauses provide that should some key costs in Government contracts rise significantly from the time of tender to the time of performance or over a long period of performance, then the contract price will escalate in accordance with some pre-agreed formula, typically with reference to an index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would protect the contractor from having to assume the risk of sharp increases in key costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will also benefit the Government in that their contractors will be under less pressure to over-budget when they bid for a contract and build into their bids their estimates for future cost increases.

sections.label: Escalation clauses and SME tenders
sections.summary: Escalation clauses remove some financial risks for contractors and may let SMEs take part in more public tenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this way, escalation clauses remove some financial risks for Government contractors and may enable or allow SMEs to punch above their weight in more public tenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To me, this would be in keeping with the spirit of this year's Budget, in the various forms of financing and tax incentives proposed to support the scale-ups of our SMEs.

sections.label: Outsourcing public sector functions
sections.summary: The Government should consider having the public sector outsource some functions in support of these organisations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The Government should consider having the public sector outsource some of their functions in support of these organisations.

sections.label: Digitalisation and e-payment use
sections.summary: The passage states that as the world transforms, Singapore must keep pace, with digitalisation one way forward, and asks whether the Ministry has advanced e-payment use.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As the world transforms, so must we, to keep pace and remain relevant with the global environment, digitalisation being one of the ways forward as there are known benefits.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: And a clarification whether the Ministry has done anything to advance the use of e-payment.

sections.label: Digitalisation and auditing processes
sections.summary: The passage asks how digitalisation changes behaviour towards auditing, security and data protection processes in organisations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, how does digitalisation change our behaviour towards the auditing, security and data protection processes in organisations?

sections.label: Unified base system structure
sections.summary: The passage states resistance to change arises when users input similar data repetitively into different Government agencies, and encourages a unified base system structure for data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Third, the resistance to change will set in when users contemplate that they have to input similar data repetitively into different Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: So, I would encourage the Government to create a unified base system structure where existing data can be shared across the different agencies.

sections.label: Those lacking resources
sections.summary: The passage states that some lack resources to keep pace, this number is expected to rise as the elderly more than double by 2030, and cites a Duke-NUS survey on caregiver support service use.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As we progress, we must not forget there are those who lack resources to keep pace.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This number is expected to rise as the number of elderly would more than double by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A Duke-NUS Medical School survey found that fewer than 5% of caregivers interviewed used individual support services, such as home nursing and respite care programmes.

sections.label: Tax credits for specialised caregivers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to consider means-tested refundable tax credits for specialised caregivers, with part going into CPF, to lessen financial burdens and improve retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, there are also specialised caregivers who feel that taking care of the dependants personally is the best care that they can give them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I ask that the Minister consider giving means-tested refundable tax credits for specialised caregivers, meaning that some of these caregivers who do not work or work part-time would get the cash refund, a portion of which would go into their Central Provident Fund (CPF).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will lessen their financial burdens, improve their retirement adequacy, give them flexibility to use Government aid and empower them to seek individual support services for a better quality of life for themselves and their loved ones.

sections.label: Eligibility assessment key factors
sections.summary: The passage states that a majority of these schemes assess eligibility based on household income, per capita income and home annual value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Currently, a majority of these schemes assess eligibility based on three broad key factors and these are: household income, per capita income and home annual value (AV).

sections.label: Means testing criteria review
sections.summary: PSEA and the CDAC top-up are entitlements for post-secondary students, and the speaker suggests reviewing the factors in means testing criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: PSEA, which is the entitlement for all post-secondary school education students, likewise, does the same, as does the CDAC top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I would suggest, Mdm Chair, that the factors which go into the means testing criteria be reviewed.

sections.label: Revising means testing criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister could consider revising means testing criteria to incorporate a matrix of factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Could the Minister consider a revision of the means testing criteria to incorporate a matrix of factors with the following in mind?

sections.label: Annual income over longer span
sections.summary: The speaker proposes considering annual income over three to five years rather than just the preceding year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Fourth, consider the annual income over a longer span of time, say, three to five years, rather than just the preceding year.

sections.label: SME compliance costs and MOF
sections.summary: The speaker says compliance costs burden SME profit margins and asks for an update on MOF plans to reduce them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet, among SMEs, compliance costs remain a significant burden on profit margins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Minister update on the Ministry of Finance’s (MOF) plans to reduce the compliance burdens on businesses?

sections.label: Consultation unit for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOF consider setting up a consultation unit to help SMEs in their first year and when policies are updated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps MOF might also want to look into setting up a consultation unit to help SMEs in this area in their first year of business operations and also when policies are updated.

sections.label: SkillsFuture apprenticeship adoption
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether SkillsFuture can push SMEs and larger companies to adopt apprenticeship or Place-and-Train schemes more pervasively.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With SkillsFuture, can we push SMEs and larger companies to adopt the apprenticeship scheme or Place-and-Train scheme more pervasively like it was in the past?

sections.label: Outcome-based procurement approach
sections.summary: Under outcome-based procurement, Government agencies are encouraged to specify desired outcomes rather than prescribe solutions in tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the outcome-based procurement approach, we encourage Government agencies to specify desired outcomes rather than prescribe solutions in their tenders.

sections.label: Shortlisted firms and sector rollout
sections.summary: Shortlisted firms need not undergo separate open tender, and outcome-based procurement is being introduced in cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Those shortlisted need not go through a separate open tender, as the objectives of fair and open competition, transparency and value for money would have already been met through the Innovation Challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are working on introducing outcome-based procurement in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors over time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, rather than specifying headcount for security contracts, agencies could specify areas to be monitored and the response time expected of security officers in the event of an alert.

sections.label: JTC and Samwoh road trial
sections.summary: JTC partnered Samwoh Corporation to trial using sedimentary rocks from Jurong Rock Caverns to pave a road outside Mediapolis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under this initiative, JTC partnered a local company, Samwoh Corporation, to successfully trial the use of sedimentary rocks excavated from the Jurong Rock Caverns to pave a stretch of road outside Mediapolis.

sections.label: SMEs securing Government projects
sections.summary: Over three years, SMEs captured more than 60% of total Government contract value and around 85% of all Government tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On helping smaller firms access Government procurement opportunities, Members will be heartened to know that over the past three years, SMEs have been successful in securing Government projects under our open procurement system, capturing more than 60% of total Government contract value and around 85% of all Government tenders.

sections.label: SMEs awarded large contracts
sections.summary: For three years, about 50% of contracts above $50 million by value were awarded to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For the past three years, by contract value, about 50% of all contracts above $50 million were awarded to SMEs, a very respectable proportion.

sections.label: Programme assistance and accreditation
sections.summary: The programme has assisted 29 companies, of which 12 have obtained accreditation status.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To date, the programme has assisted 29 companies, of which 12 have obtained accreditation status.

sections.label: Contracts awarded to accredited companies
sections.summary: More than 15 contracts have been awarded to accredited companies, with many more in discussions towards signing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: More than 15 contracts have been awarded to accredited companies and many more are currently in various stages of discussions towards signing of a contract.

sections.label: Accreditation to combat cheap sourcing
sections.summary: The Government decided to accredit or license companies paying according to the Progressive Wage Model and buy only from them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To combat the risk of cheap sourcing and suppressed wages in these sectors, and following agreement with our tripartite partners, the Government took a deliberate decision to accredit or license companies that pay according to the Progressive Wage Model and to buy only from these companies in these sectors.

sections.label: Ease of Doing Business ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranked No 1 in the World Bank Group's Ease of Doing Business Index for 10 years, and ACRA changed the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As Mr Saktiandi noted, Singapore has been ranked No 1 in the World Bank Group's Ease of Doing Business Index for the past 10 years, ahead of other countries, such as Korea, Japan and the United States.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the past year, ACRA has implemented significant changes to the Companies Act to reduce the regulatory burden, provide greater business flexibility and improve the corporate governance standards in Singapore.

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Panel suggestions reviewed
sections.summary: The Pro-Enterprise Panel has reviewed over 1,800 suggestions, and more than half led to changes in regulations and rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Since its inception, the Pro-Enterprise Panel has reviewed more than 1,800 suggestions and more than half have led to changes in regulations and rules.

sections.label: Outreach to 2,000 businesses
sections.summary: Feedback has been generally positive, and outreach efforts will be ramped up to another 2,000 businesses this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Feedback has been generally positive, and we intend to ramp up our outreach efforts to another 2,000 businesses this year.

sections.label: Grants and corporate regulatory regime
sections.summary: The application process for SPRING's Capability Development Grants below $30,000 was simplified, and the Business Grants Portal was launched.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In last year's Budget, we simplified the application process for SPRING's Capability Development Grants below $30,000 by reducing the information required.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, of course, Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the launch of the Business Grants Portal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We must continue to ensure financial prudence, but we must also be fair to our companies and their workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will also continue to review our corporate regulatory regime to ensure that it remains relevant while facilitating ease of doing business in Singapore.

sections.label: e-Government satisfaction survey 2015
sections.summary: A 2015 IDA survey found almost three in four citizens were very or extremely satisfied with completing Government e-services online.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The IDA's e-Government Perception Survey conducted in 2015 indicated that almost three in four citizens were very satisfied or extremely satisfied with the ease of completing transactions online using Government e-services.

sections.label: Employers renewing directly with MOM
sections.summary: More employers now interface directly with MOM, with 56% of renewals done directly in the past 12 months, up 11 percentage points.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Instead of relying on agents, more employers now directly interface with MOM, with 56% of renewals done directly by employers in the past 12 months, up by 11 percentage points from a year earlier.

sections.label: NEHR users and record searches
sections.summary: In March 2016, there were over 11,400 NEHR users and more than 600,000 searches for patient records.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the month of March 2016, there were more than 11,400 users of NEHR and over 600,000 searches made for patient records.

sections.label: IRAS electronic tax filing savings
sections.summary: IRAS saved taxpayer time through electronic tax-filing and no-filing schemes and redeployed around 100 officers despite 32% tax base growth from 2009 to 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For example, through the electronic tax-filing and no-filing schemes, IRAS has saved time for taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It was also able to redeploy around 100 officers who used to handle manual tax filings to new and other areas of work, despite the tax base growth of 32% from 2009 to 2014.

sections.label: Internet use among older individuals
sections.summary: IDA surveys showed three in four aged 50 to 59 and almost one in three aged 60 and above used the Internet in 2014, up from two years before.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Based on IDA's surveys, three in four individuals aged 50 to 59, and almost one in three seniors aged 60 and above used the Internet in 2014, with usage increasing considerably compared to two years ago.

sections.label: CCCs upgrading to CCC+
sections.summary: CCCs helped around 120,000 citizens access e-services in 2015, and will be upgraded to CCC+s starting with pilots, then nationwide from 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2015, CCCs helped around 120,000 citizens to access e-services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will enhance our CCCs to make it even easier for users to self-help by upgrading the equipment and redesigning the online interfaces.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will progressively upgrade the CCCs to become CCC+s, starting with pilots at the Toa Payoh Central and Chong Pang CCCs, and Our Tampines Hub by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If successful, the nationwide rollout of CCC+s will follow from 2017 onwards.

sections.label: FDW levy and grant
sections.summary: Caregivers who hire a FDW may get a lower concessionary levy, and lower- and middle-income families caring for an elderly person or a person with moderate disabilities may get an additional FDW grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If caregivers hire a FDW, they can benefit from a lower FDW concessionary levy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If they are from lower- and middle-income families and are caring for an elderly person or a person with moderate disabilities, they can get an additional FDW grant.

sections.label: Wealth measure as proxy
sections.summary: It is not a perfect measure for wealth but remains the best available proxy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: While it is not a perfect measure for wealth, it remains the best available proxy.

sections.label: Means-testing criteria review
sections.summary: It is similar to the UK's Income Support, and means-testing criteria across all schemes will continue to be reviewed to target assistance at those who need it most.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is more similar to the UK's Income Support mentioned by the Member.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will continue to review our means-testing criteria across all schemes to ensure that our assistance is targeted at those who need them most.

sections.label: CCC+ kiosks and landing pages
sections.summary: CCC+ kiosks comprise docked mobile tablets with touch-screen interfaces, some height-adjustable for wheelchair users, and CCC+ landing pages would be redesigned for access to the 10 most commonly used digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The CCC+s that I have talked about earlier, are kiosks which will comprise docked mobile tablets with touch-screen interfaces, that are less cumbersome and easier for the elderly to use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Some kiosks will also be height-adjustable to better serve the needs of those who are wheelchair bound.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In addition, CCC+ landing pages would be redesigned for better access to the 10 most commonly used digital services by CCC visitors today, such as checking their CPF and IRAS statements.

sections.label: Interim expenditure under Constitution
sections.summary: The Government can continue operations as per normal because Article 148 of the Constitution allows expenditures in the interim until the Supply Bill is passed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Government is able to continue its operations as per normal because Article 148 of the Constitution allows for expenditures in the interim until the Supply Bill is passed.
